A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Poisson SGD research. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained proofs and the relocated trajectory illustration.

before.justification: Figure 1 reports original simulated SGD and Poisson SGD trajectories on a quartic objective, showing local-minimum trapping and escape. These qualify despite the absence of a dedicated experiments section.

after.justification: Section 7 and Figures 3–5 report original synthetic convergence experiments and neural-network classification results, alongside the retained trajectory illustration.

M1.justification: Section 3 adds C_alpha to the reflective momentum coefficient, introducing an additional gradient contribution used with positive values in experiments. Algorithm 1 also explicitly wraps parameter updates modulo a. These change the update procedure; the theoretical analysis retains C_alpha = 0.

E1.justification: The original quartic optimization example is retained. Section 7 adds a synthetic two-dimensional regression/convergence setting and image classification on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, substantially expanding actual evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's SGD comparator, Figure 5 evaluates momentum SGD and SGLD on MNIST and CIFAR-10, and Adam on CIFAR-100 with ResNet18. The retained illustration's SGD/Poisson SGD labels become GD/Poisson GD to identify full-batch operation; this relabeling alone is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Wasserstein-distance evaluation over training epochs and training/validation error comparisons across four network configurations. Appendix A.2 specifies new protocols, including 10,000 synthetic observations with batch size 100, classification splits, and batch sizes 128 or 256.

E4.justification: Section 7.1 adds a targeted investigation of the stationary-distribution mechanism: parameter distributions at 10, 100, and 1000 epochs and Wasserstein-distance trajectories against SGD. Figures 3–4 provide substantially more diagnostic evidence than the retained local-versus-global trajectory example.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The added curves and parameter clouds do not introduce a stated uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The original trajectory finding is retained as Figure 2. New Figures 3–4 report concentration around the synthetic minimizer set and decreasing Wasserstein distance for Poisson SGD compared with approximately stable SGD distance. Figure 5 adds training and validation error curves for four dataset/network combinations.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 restricts the formerly general compact parameter space, exemplified by a torus or sphere, to a torus, changing the scope of the theory. Remarks 3–4 add covariance-rank and learning-rate variance arguments. Theorem 5 changes a logarithmic constant without a corresponding change in Appendix E. Most principal proofs remain intact; Appendix H restates previously invoked results.

C1.justification: The abstract and stated contributions retain the same central claims: stationary-distribution convergence despite degenerate update directions, global optimization, and generalization analysis through a BPS/PDMP connection. The experiments supply additional evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds a flat-minimum preference interpretation, motivates the torus restriction, acknowledges tuning of the trajectory example, and distinguishes positive C_alpha in practice from zero in theory. It also replaces ReLU with Tanh in its smooth-network examples and specifies constant-learning-rate SGD as a future direction.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.2 supplies synthetic-data generation, architecture descriptions, dataset splits, batch sizes, optimizer parameters, and Poisson SGD hyperparameters. Section 3 newly discloses the retained illustration's learning rate and hyperparameters, while Section 2 explicitly specifies sampling with replacement.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 explicitly contrasts the learning-rate designs and objectives of this work with Musso and Blier et al. V2 also adds citations concerning gradient noise, torus-based analysis, and the evaluated datasets and architectures. The central positioning relative to SGLD and BPS remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The existing exposition and proof sequence are largely retained, with expanded introductory explanations, additional remarks, and a revised concluding outlook. Structural edits add an experiments section and appendix subsections and move references before the appendices, without extensively rewriting the retained narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the TMLR layout with redesigned headings, author information, running headers, and denser typesetting. It adds a conceptual schematic and three experimental figures, including a four-panel comparison. The original trajectory plot is resized and relocated with a side caption.

improvement.justification: Section 7 and Appendix A.2 add useful empirical evidence and concrete experimental settings beyond v1's single trajectory plot, while applicability explanations become clearer. The gain is limited because experiments with positive C_alpha do not directly validate the zero-C_alpha theory, and v2 introduces a constant inconsistency between Theorem 5 and its Appendix E proof.
